 32        distance_function: str | DistanceFunction = "rmsd",
 33        **distance_kwargs: Any,
 34    ):
 35        """
 36        Initialize the CriticalPointGraph.
 37
 38        Parameters:
 39        threshold: Distance threshold for uniqueness checking (default: 0.1)
 40        distance_function: Distance function to use ('rmsd', 'euclidean', 'max_coordinate')
 41                          or a custom DistanceFunction callable
 42        **distance_kwargs: Additional arguments passed to the distance function
 43        """
 44        self._graph = nx.DiGraph()
 45        self.threshold = threshold
 46
 47        # Configure distance function
 48        if isinstance(distance_function, str):
 49            self.distance_function = DistanceRegistry.create(distance_function)
 50            self.distance_function_name = distance_function
 51        else:
 52            self.distance_function = distance_function
 53            self.distance_function_name = getattr(
 54                distance_function, "__name__", "custom"
 55            )
 56
 57        self.distance_kwargs = distance_kwargs
 58
 59    @property
 60    def graph(self) -> nx.DiGraph:
 61        """Access the underlying NetworkX graph."""
 62        return self._graph
 63
 64    def add(self, critical_point: CriticalPoint) -> bool:
 65        """
 66        Add a critical point to the graph only if it's not similar to existing nodes.
 67
 68        Parameters:
 69        critical_point: CriticalPoint object to add
 70
 71        Returns:
 72        bool: True if added, False if similar to existing node
 73        """
 74        new_xyz = critical_point.xyz
 75
 76        logger.debug("Attempting to add critical point:")
 77        logger.debug(f"  Index: {critical_point.index}")
 78        logger.debug(f"  Energy: {critical_point.energy:.6f}")
 79        logger.debug(f"  Position: {critical_point.state}")
 80        logger.debug(f"  XYZ key: {new_xyz}")
 81        logger.debug(f"  Distance function: {self.distance_function_name}")
 82        logger.debug(f"  Threshold: {self.threshold}")
 83
 84        # Check if this exact XYZ already exists
 85        if new_xyz in self._graph.nodes:
 86            existing_point = self._graph.nodes[new_xyz]["data"]
 87            logger.debug("Exact XYZ match found - point already exists!")
 88            logger.debug(
 89                f"  Existing point: index={existing_point.index}, energy={existing_point.energy:.6f}"
 90            )
 91            logger.debug(
 92                f"Critical point with identical XYZ already exists (index: {existing_point.index})"
 93            )
 94            return False
 95
 96        logger.debug(
 97            f"No exact XYZ match. Checking similarity with {len(self._graph.nodes)} existing nodes:"
 98        )
 99
100        # Check similarity with all existing nodes
101        for existing_xyz in self._graph.nodes:
102            existing_point = self._graph.nodes[existing_xyz]["data"]
103            logger.debug("  Comparing with existing node:")
104            logger.debug(f"    Existing XYZ: {existing_xyz}")
105            logger.debug(
106                f"    Existing point: index={existing_point.index}, energy={existing_point.energy:.6f}, position={existing_point.state}"
107            )
108
109            distance = self.distance_function(
110                new_xyz, existing_xyz, **self.distance_kwargs
111            )
112            logger.debug(f"    Distance computed: {distance:.8f}")
113            logger.debug(f"    Threshold: {self.threshold}")
114            logger.debug(f"    Distance <= threshold: {distance <= self.threshold}")
115
116            # Debug: Parse coordinates to verify
117            from ..common.distance import get_coordinates_xyz_lines
118
119            lines1 = new_xyz.strip().split("\n")
120            lines2 = existing_xyz.strip().split("\n")
121            atoms1, coords1 = get_coordinates_xyz_lines(lines1)
122            atoms2, coords2 = get_coordinates_xyz_lines(lines2)
123            logger.debug(f"    New coords: {coords1}")
124            logger.debug(f"    Existing coords: {coords2}")
125            logger.debug(
126                f"    Manual distance: {np.linalg.norm(coords1 - coords2):.8f}"
127            )
128
129            if distance <= self.threshold:
130                logger.debug("DEBUG: Point is too similar - NOT adding to graph!")
131                logger.debug(
132                    f"  Reason: distance {distance:.8f} <= threshold {self.threshold}"
133                )
134                logger.debug(
135                    f"Critical point too similar to existing node (distance: {distance:.4f}, index: {existing_point.index})"
136                )
137                return False
138
139        # If we get here, the point is unique enough - add it
140        logger.debug("DEBUG: Point is unique enough - adding to graph!")
141        self._graph.add_node(new_xyz, data=critical_point)
142        logger.debug(
143            f"Added unique critical point (index: {critical_point.index}, energy: {critical_point.energy:.4f})"
144        )
145        return True
146
147    def find_similar(
148        self, target_point: CriticalPoint, threshold: float = None
149    ) -> List[Tuple[str, float, CriticalPoint]]:
150        """
151        Find all points in the graph similar to the target point.
152
153        Parameters:
154        target_point: CriticalPoint to compare against
155        threshold: Distance threshold (uses instance threshold if None)
156
157        Returns:
158        list: List of (xyz_key, distance_value, critical_point) tuples for similar structures
159        """
160        if threshold is None:
161            threshold = self.threshold
162
163        target_xyz = target_point.xyz
164        similar = []
165
166        for node_xyz in self._graph.nodes:
167            if node_xyz == target_xyz:
168                continue  # Skip self-comparison
169
170            distance = self.distance_function(
171                target_xyz, node_xyz, **self.distance_kwargs
172            )
173            if distance <= threshold:
174                similar.append(
175                    (node_xyz, distance, self._graph.nodes[node_xyz]["data"])
176                )
177
178        return sorted(similar, key=lambda x: x[1])  # Sort by distance
179
180    def check_uniqueness(self, threshold: float = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
181        """
182        Check the graph for similar structures and report duplicates.
183
184        Parameters:
185        threshold: Distance threshold for similarity (uses instance threshold if None)
186
187        Returns:
188        dict: Dictionary with duplicate information
189        """
190        if threshold is None:
191            threshold = self.threshold
192
193        nodes_list = list(self._graph.nodes)
194        duplicates = []
195
196        logger.debug(f"Checking uniqueness of {len(nodes_list)} nodes...")
197
198        for i, xyz1 in enumerate(nodes_list):
199            for xyz2 in nodes_list[i + 1 :]:
200                distance = self.distance_function(xyz1, xyz2, **self.distance_kwargs)
201                if distance <= threshold:
202                    point1 = self._graph.nodes[xyz1]["data"]
203                    point2 = self._graph.nodes[xyz2]["data"]
204                    duplicates.append(
205                        {
206                            "distance": distance,
207                            "point1": {"index": point1.index, "energy": point1.energy},
208                            "point2": {"index": point2.index, "energy": point2.energy},
209                        }
210                    )
211                    logger.debug(
212                        f"Duplicate found: distance {distance:.4f} between indices {point1.index} and {point2.index}"
213                    )
214
215        result = {
216            "total_nodes": len(nodes_list),
217            "duplicates_found": len(duplicates),
218            "duplicates": duplicates,
219        }
220
221        logger.debug("\nSummary:")
222        logger.debug(f"- Total nodes: {result['total_nodes']}")
223        logger.debug(f"- Duplicate pairs: {result['duplicates_found']}")
224
225        return result
226
227    def save(self, filepath: str) -> None:
228        """Save the graph to a JSON file."""
229        import json
230        import logging
231
232        logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
233
234        graph_data = self.to_config()
235
236        # Save to JSON
237        with open(filepath, "w") as f:
238            json.dump(graph_data, f, indent=2)
239
240        logger.debug(f"Saved CriticalPointGraph to {filepath} (JSON format)")
241
242    def to_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
243        """Serialize the graph to a configuration dictionary."""
244
245        # Prepare graph data
246        graph_data = {
247            "threshold": self.threshold,
248            "distance_function": self.distance_function_name,
249            "distance_kwargs": self.distance_kwargs,
250            "nodes": {},
251            "edges": [],
252        }
253
254        # Serialize nodes with CriticalPoint data
255        for node_id, node_data in self._graph.nodes(data=True):
256            critical_point = node_data["data"]
257            graph_data["nodes"][node_id] = critical_point.to_config()
258
259        # Serialize edges
260        for u, v, edge_data in self._graph.edges(data=True):
261            # Process edge data to handle SerialisableDataClass objects
262            processed_edge_data = {}
263            for key, value in edge_data.items():
264                if hasattr(value, "to_config"):  # Check if it's a SerialisableDataClass
265                    processed_edge_data[key] = value.to_config()
266                else:
267                    processed_edge_data[key] = value
268
269            graph_data["edges"].append(
270                {"source": u, "target": v, "data": processed_edge_data}
271            )
272
273        return graph_data
274
275    @classmethod
276    def from_config(cls, graph_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> "CriticalPointGraph":
277        """Create CriticalPointGraph from configuration dictionary."""
278
279        # Create new graph instance
280        graph = cls(
281            threshold=graph_data["threshold"],
282            distance_function=graph_data.get("distance_function", "rmsd"),
283            **graph_data.get("distance_kwargs", {}),
284        )
285
286        # Deserialize nodes
287        for node_id, node_config in graph_data["nodes"].items():
288            critical_point = CriticalPoint.from_config(node_config)
289            graph._graph.add_node(node_id, data=critical_point)
290
291        # Deserialize edges
292        for edge_data in graph_data["edges"]:
293            # Process edge data to reconstruct SerialisableDataClass objects
294            processed_edge_data = {}
295            for key, value in edge_data["data"].items():
296                if isinstance(value, dict) and "_class" in value:
297                    # Import the class dynamically
298                    module_name = value["_module"]
299                    class_name = value["_class"]
300                    module = __import__(module_name, fromlist=[class_name])
301                    item_class = getattr(module, class_name)
302                    processed_edge_data[key] = item_class.from_config(value)
303                else:
304                    processed_edge_data[key] = value
305
306            graph._graph.add_edge(
307                edge_data["source"], edge_data["target"], **processed_edge_data
308            )
309
310        return graph
311
312    # Delegate other NetworkX methods to the underlying graph
313    def __getattr__(self, name):
314        """Delegate attribute access to the underlying NetworkX graph."""
315        return getattr(self._graph, name)
316
317    def __len__(self):
318        """Return the number of nodes in the graph."""
319        return len(self._graph)
320
321    def __iter__(self):
322        """Iterate over the nodes in the graph."""
323        return iter(self._graph)
324
325    def __contains__(self, item):
326        """Check if item is in the graph nodes."""
327        return item in self._graph
328
329    def report(self) -> str:
330        """
331        Generate a comprehensive summary report of the graph status.
332
333        Returns:
334            str: Formatted report string with graph statistics
335        """
336        lines = []
337        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
338        lines.append("CRITICAL POINT GRAPH STATUS SUMMARY")
339        lines.append("=" * 80)
340
341        # Basic graph statistics
342        total_nodes = len(self._graph.nodes)
343        total_edges = len(self._graph.edges)
344        lines.append("\nGraph Structure:")
345        lines.append(f"  Total nodes: {total_nodes}")
346        lines.append(f"  Total edges: {total_edges}")
347        lines.append(f"  Distance function: {self.distance_function_name}")
348        lines.append(f"  Distance threshold: {self.threshold}")
349        if self.distance_kwargs:
350            lines.append(f"  Distance kwargs: {self.distance_kwargs}")
351
352        # Node analysis by Morse index
353        if total_nodes > 0:
354            index_counts = {}
355            energy_stats = {"min": float("inf"), "max": float("-inf"), "sum": 0.0}
356            points_by_index = []
357
358            for node_id, node_data in self._graph.nodes(data=True):
359                point = node_data["data"]
360                index = point.index
361                energy = point.energy
362
363                # Count by index
364                if index not in index_counts:
365                    index_counts[index] = []
366                index_counts[index].append((point, energy))
367
368                # Energy statistics
369                energy_stats["min"] = min(energy_stats["min"], energy)
370                energy_stats["max"] = max(energy_stats["max"], energy)
371                energy_stats["sum"] += energy
372
373                points_by_index.append((index, energy, point.state))
374
375            # Sort points by index for display
376            points_by_index.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
377
378            lines.append("\nNodes by Morse index:")
379            for index in sorted(index_counts.keys()):
380                count = len(index_counts[index])
381                energies = [e for _, e in index_counts[index]]
382                min_energy = min(energies)
383                max_energy = max(energies)
384                lines.append(
385                    f"  Index {index}: {count} points - Energy range: [{min_energy:.4f}, {max_energy:.4f}]"
386                )
387
388                # Show first few points for this index
389                if count <= 3:
390                    for point, energy in index_counts[index][:3]:
391                        coords = [round(float(c), 1) for c in point.state]
392                        lines.append(
393                            f"    [{coords[0]} {coords[1]} {coords[2]}] (E={energy:.4f})"
394                        )
395                else:
396                    for point, energy in index_counts[index][:2]:
397                        coords = [round(float(c), 1) for c in point.state]
398                        lines.append(
399                            f"    [{coords[0]} {coords[1]} {coords[2]}] (E={energy:.4f})"
400                        )
401                    lines.append(f"    ... (+{count-2} more)")
402
403            lines.append("\nEnergy Statistics:")
404            lines.append(
405                f"  Energy range: [{energy_stats['min']:.4f}, {energy_stats['max']:.4f}]"
406            )
407            lines.append(
408                f"  Energy span: {energy_stats['max'] - energy_stats['min']:.4f}"
409            )
410            lines.append(f"  Average energy: {energy_stats['sum'] / total_nodes:.4f}")
411
412        # Edge connectivity analysis
413        if total_edges > 0:
414            lines.append("\nConnectivity Analysis:")
415            degrees = [deg for _, deg in self._graph.degree()]
416            if degrees:
417                lines.append(f"  Average degree: {sum(degrees) / len(degrees):.2f}")
418                lines.append(f"  Max degree: {max(degrees)}")
419                lines.append(f"  Min degree: {min(degrees)}")
420
421            # Edge weight statistics
422            edge_weights = []
423            for _, _, edge_data in self._graph.edges(data=True):
424                if "distance" in edge_data:
425                    edge_weights.append(edge_data["distance"])
426                elif "weight" in edge_data:
427                    edge_weights.append(edge_data["weight"])
428
429            if edge_weights:
430                lines.append(
431                    f"  Edge weight range: [{min(edge_weights):.4f}, {max(edge_weights):.4f}]"
432                )
433                lines.append(
434                    f"  Average edge weight: {sum(edge_weights) / len(edge_weights):.4f}"
435                )
436
437        lines.append("=" * 80)
438        return "\n".join(lines)

260        for u, v, edge_data in self._graph.edges(data=True):
261            # Process edge data to handle SerialisableDataClass objects
262            processed_edge_data = {}
263            for key, value in edge_data.items():
264                if hasattr(value, "to_config"):  # Check if it's a SerialisableDataClass
265                    processed_edge_data[key] = value.to_config()
266                else:
267                    processed_edge_data[key] = value
268
269            graph_data["edges"].append(
270                {"source": u, "target": v, "data": processed_edge_data}
271            )
272
273        return graph_data

Serialize the graph to a configuration dictionary.

@classmethod
def from_config( cls, graph_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> CriticalPointGraph: 
275    @classmethod
276    def from_config(cls, graph_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> "CriticalPointGraph":
277        """Create CriticalPointGraph from configuration dictionary."""
278
279        # Create new graph instance
280        graph = cls(
281            threshold=graph_data["threshold"],
282            distance_function=graph_data.get("distance_function", "rmsd"),
283            **graph_data.get("distance_kwargs", {}),
284        )
285
286        # Deserialize nodes
287        for node_id, node_config in graph_data["nodes"].items():
288            critical_point = CriticalPoint.from_config(node_config)
289            graph._graph.add_node(node_id, data=critical_point)
290
291        # Deserialize edges
292        for edge_data in graph_data["edges"]:
293            # Process edge data to reconstruct SerialisableDataClass objects
294            processed_edge_data = {}
295            for key, value in edge_data["data"].items():
296                if isinstance(value, dict) and "_class" in value:
297                    # Import the class dynamically
298                    module_name = value["_module"]
299                    class_name = value["_class"]
300                    module = __import__(module_name, fromlist=[class_name])
301                    item_class = getattr(module, class_name)
302                    processed_edge_data[key] = item_class.from_config(value)
303                else:
304                    processed_edge_data[key] = value
305
306            graph._graph.add_edge(
307                edge_data["source"], edge_data["target"], **processed_edge_data
308            )
309
310        return graph

def report(self) -> str: 
329    def report(self) -> str:
330        """
331        Generate a comprehensive summary report of the graph status.
332
333        Returns:
334            str: Formatted report string with graph statistics
335        """
336        lines = []
337        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
338        lines.append("CRITICAL POINT GRAPH STATUS SUMMARY")
339        lines.append("=" * 80)
340
341        # Basic graph statistics
342        total_nodes = len(self._graph.nodes)
343        total_edges = len(self._graph.edges)
344        lines.append("\nGraph Structure:")
345        lines.append(f"  Total nodes: {total_nodes}")
346        lines.append(f"  Total edges: {total_edges}")
347        lines.append(f"  Distance function: {self.distance_function_name}")
348        lines.append(f"  Distance threshold: {self.threshold}")
349        if self.distance_kwargs:
350            lines.append(f"  Distance kwargs: {self.distance_kwargs}")
351
352        # Node analysis by Morse index
353        if total_nodes > 0:
354            index_counts = {}
355            energy_stats = {"min": float("inf"), "max": float("-inf"), "sum": 0.0}
356            points_by_index = []
357
358            for node_id, node_data in self._graph.nodes(data=True):
359                point = node_data["data"]
360                index = point.index
361                energy = point.energy
362
363                # Count by index
364                if index not in index_counts:
365                    index_counts[index] = []
366                index_counts[index].append((point, energy))
367
368                # Energy statistics
369                energy_stats["min"] = min(energy_stats["min"], energy)
370                energy_stats["max"] = max(energy_stats["max"], energy)
371                energy_stats["sum"] += energy
372
373                points_by_index.append((index, energy, point.state))
374
375            # Sort points by index for display
376            points_by_index.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
377
378            lines.append("\nNodes by Morse index:")
379            for index in sorted(index_counts.keys()):
380                count = len(index_counts[index])
381                energies = [e for _, e in index_counts[index]]
382                min_energy = min(energies)
383                max_energy = max(energies)
384                lines.append(
385                    f"  Index {index}: {count} points - Energy range: [{min_energy:.4f}, {max_energy:.4f}]"
386                )
387
388                # Show first few points for this index
389                if count <= 3:
390                    for point, energy in index_counts[index][:3]:
391                        coords = [round(float(c), 1) for c in point.state]
392                        lines.append(
393                            f"    [{coords[0]} {coords[1]} {coords[2]}] (E={energy:.4f})"
394                        )
395                else:
396                    for point, energy in index_counts[index][:2]:
397                        coords = [round(float(c), 1) for c in point.state]
398                        lines.append(
399                            f"    [{coords[0]} {coords[1]} {coords[2]}] (E={energy:.4f})"
400                        )
401                    lines.append(f"    ... (+{count-2} more)")
402
403            lines.append("\nEnergy Statistics:")
404            lines.append(
405                f"  Energy range: [{energy_stats['min']:.4f}, {energy_stats['max']:.4f}]"
406            )
407            lines.append(
408                f"  Energy span: {energy_stats['max'] - energy_stats['min']:.4f}"
409            )
410            lines.append(f"  Average energy: {energy_stats['sum'] / total_nodes:.4f}")
411
412        # Edge connectivity analysis
413        if total_edges > 0:
414            lines.append("\nConnectivity Analysis:")
415            degrees = [deg for _, deg in self._graph.degree()]
416            if degrees:
417                lines.append(f"  Average degree: {sum(degrees) / len(degrees):.2f}")
418                lines.append(f"  Max degree: {max(degrees)}")
419                lines.append(f"  Min degree: {min(degrees)}")
420
421            # Edge weight statistics
422            edge_weights = []
423            for _, _, edge_data in self._graph.edges(data=True):
424                if "distance" in edge_data:
425                    edge_weights.append(edge_data["distance"])
426                elif "weight" in edge_data:
427                    edge_weights.append(edge_data["weight"])
428
429            if edge_weights:
430                lines.append(
431                    f"  Edge weight range: [{min(edge_weights):.4f}, {max(edge_weights):.4f}]"
432                )
433                lines.append(
434                    f"  Average edge weight: {sum(edge_weights) / len(edge_weights):.4f}"
435                )
436
437        lines.append("=" * 80)
438        return "\n".join(lines)

461    def _get_search_state(self, search_procedure: str) -> Dict[str, Set[str]]:
462        """Get or create search state for a procedure."""
463        if search_procedure not in self._search_states:
464            self._search_states[search_procedure] = {
465                "processed_nodes": set(),
466            }
467        return self._search_states[search_procedure]
468
469    def mark_processed(self, node_id: str, search_procedure: str) -> None:
470        """
471        Mark a node as processed by a specific search procedure.
472
473        Parameters:
474        node_id: Node identifier (XYZ string)
475        search_procedure: Name of the search procedure (e.g., 'upward', 'downward')
476        """
477        if node_id in self._graph.nodes:
478            state = self._get_search_state(search_procedure)
479            state["processed_nodes"].add(node_id)
480        else:
481            logger.warning(
482                f"mark_processed({search_procedure}): node {node_id[:50]}... not in graph, not marking"
483            )
484
485    def is_processed(self, node_id: str, search_procedure: str) -> bool:
486        """
487        Check if a node has been processed by a specific search procedure.
488
489        Parameters:
490        node_id: Node identifier (XYZ string)
491        search_procedure: Name of the search procedure
492
493        Returns:
494        bool: True if processed by this procedure
495        """
496        state = self._get_search_state(search_procedure)
497        return node_id in state["processed_nodes"]
498
499    def get_unprocessed_nodes(self, search_procedure: str) -> Set[str]:
500        """
501        Get all nodes that haven't been processed by a specific search procedure.
502
503        Parameters:
504        search_procedure: Name of the search procedure
505
506        Returns:
507        Set of node IDs that are unprocessed by this procedure
508        """
509        state = self._get_search_state(search_procedure)
510        all_nodes = set(self._graph.nodes)
511        processed = state["processed_nodes"]
512        unprocessed = all_nodes - processed
513        return unprocessed
514
515    def get_next_to_process(self, search_procedure: str) -> str:
516        """
517        Get the next unprocessed node for a specific search procedure (FIFO strategy).
518
519        Parameters:
520        search_procedure: Name of the search procedure
521
522        Returns:
523        str: Next node ID to process, or None if no unprocessed nodes
524        """
525        unprocessed = self.get_unprocessed_nodes(search_procedure)
526        return next(iter(unprocessed)) if unprocessed else None

542        state = self._get_search_state(search_procedure)

545        unprocessed = total_nodes - processed
546
547        return {
548            "total_nodes": total_nodes,

550            "unprocessed": unprocessed,

633                lines.append("\nSearch Procedure Status:")
634                lines.append("  No search procedures registered yet")
635
636        return "\n".join(lines)

@SearchOrchestratorRegistry.register('serial')
class SearchOrchestrator: 
 54@SearchOrchestratorRegistry.register("serial")
 55class SearchOrchestrator:
 56    """
 57    Main orchestrator for search algorithms.
 58
 59    This class coordinates the entire search process, managing job queues,
 60    node states, and job execution according to the specified algorithm.
 61    """
 62
 63    def __init__(
 64        self,
 65        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
 66        job_queues: JobQueues,
 67        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
 68        d_max: Optional[int] = None,
 69        perturbation_magnitude: float = 0.1,
 70        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
 71    ):
 72        """
 73        Initialize the search orchestrator.
 74
 75        Args:
 76            graph: The searchable graph to work with
 77            job_queues: The job queues for managing pending jobs
 78            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner for executing jobs
 79            d_max: Maximum search order (index) for upward search. If None, no limit is applied.
 80            perturbation_magnitude: Default magnitude for perturbations when spawning jobs
 81            callbacks: Optional callbacks instance to be notified after job batch execution
 82        """
 83        self.graph = graph
 84        self.job_queues = job_queues
 85        self.d_max = d_max
 86        self.job_tracker = JobTracker()
 87        self.node_states = NodeStateManager(graph)
 88        self.executor = JobExecutor(hisd_runner, max_concurrent=1)  # Start with serial
 89
 90        # Search parameters
 91        self.perturbation_magnitude = perturbation_magnitude
 92
 93        # Use composition with strategies (configured with default perturbation magnitude)
 94        self.upward_strategy = FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy(
 95            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
 96        )
 97        self.downward_strategy = ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy(
 98            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
 99        )
100
101        # Callbacks for job batch completion
102        self.callbacks = callbacks
103
104        # Statistics and monitoring
105        self.monitor: SearchMonitor = SearchMonitor()
106
107    def run_upward_search(self) -> None:
108        """
109        Run the upward search algorithm using the upward strategy's configured
110        `perturbation_magnitude` that was set when the orchestrator was
111        initialized.
112        """
113        self.run_search(self.upward_strategy, "upward")
114
115    def run_search(self, strategy: "SearchStrategy", procedure: str) -> None:
116        """
117        Run a search using the given strategy.
118
119        Args:
120            strategy: The search strategy to use
121            procedure: The search procedure ("upward" or "downward")
122        """
123        self._initialize_search(procedure)
124
125        while not self._is_search_finished(procedure):
126            # For each unprocessed node, ask the strategy which RunConditions to spawn
127            unprocessed_nodes = self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
128            logger.debug(f"Found {len(unprocessed_nodes)} unprocessed nodes")
129
130            for node_id in unprocessed_nodes:
131                if node_id not in self.graph._graph.nodes:
132                    logger.warning(f"Node {node_id} not found in graph")
133                    self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
134                    continue
135
136                node_data = self.graph._graph.nodes[node_id]["data"]
137
138                # Delegation: strategy returns RunCondition objects for this critical point
139                try:
140                    run_conditions = strategy.spawn_jobs(node_data)
141                except Exception as e:
142                    logger.error(f"Strategy.spawn_jobs failed for node {node_id}: {e}")
143                    run_conditions = []
144
145                # Create job ids and register jobs
146                jobs: List[tuple[str, RunCondition]] = []
147                for idx, rc in enumerate(run_conditions):
148                    job_id = f"{node_id}_{procedure}_{idx}"
149                    jobs.append((job_id, rc))
150
151                # Add to queues and tracker
152                self.job_queues.add_jobs(procedure, jobs)
153                job_ids = [job_id for job_id, _ in jobs]
154                self.job_tracker.add_jobs_for_node(node_id, job_ids)
155                # Mark node processed immediately after spawning and registering jobs
156                self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
157
158            # Execute pending jobs and log progress
159            self._execute_pending_jobs(procedure)
160            self._log_progress(procedure)
161
162        self._finalize_search(procedure)
163
164    def _initialize_search(self, procedure: str) -> None:
165        """Initialize search state."""
166        logger.debug(f"Starting {procedure} search")
167        if procedure == "upward" and self.d_max is not None:
168            logger.debug(f"Maximum search order (d_max): {self.d_max}")
169
170        # Start monitoring the search
171        self.monitor.start_search(procedure)
172
173    def _is_search_finished(self, procedure: str) -> bool:
174        """Check if search is complete."""
175        return self.job_queues.is_queue_empty(
176            procedure
177        ) and not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
178
179    def _spawn_jobs_for_unprocessed_nodes(self, procedure: str) -> None:
180        """Spawn jobs for unprocessed nodes."""
181        unprocessed_nodes = self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
182        logger.debug(f"Found {len(unprocessed_nodes)} unprocessed nodes")
183
184        for node_id in unprocessed_nodes:
185            jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(node_id, procedure)
186
187            if jobs:
188                self.job_queues.add_jobs(procedure, jobs)
189                logger.debug(f"Spawned {len(jobs)} jobs for node {node_id}")
190                # Trigger callbacks after spawning jobs to allow checkpointing
191                if self.callbacks is not None:
192                    for callback in self.callbacks:
193                        callback.on_job_complete(self)
194            else:
195                # No jobs spawned - mark as processed immediately
196                self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
197                logger.debug(f"Node {node_id} marked as processed (no jobs to spawn)")
198
199    def _execute_pending_jobs(self, procedure: str) -> None:
200        """Execute all pending jobs in the queue."""
201        jobs_to_execute = self.job_queues.clear_queue(procedure)
202
203        if jobs_to_execute:
204            logger.debug(f"Executing {len(jobs_to_execute)} jobs")
205
206            for job_id, run_condition in jobs_to_execute:
207                # Execute the job
208                result = self.executor.execute_job(run_condition, job_id)
209
210                # Record job completion in monitor
211                self.monitor.record_job_completion(
212                    procedure=procedure,
213                    job_id=job_id,
214                    success=result.success,
215                    execution_time=result.execution_time,
216                    node_id=(
217                        run_condition.node_id
218                        if hasattr(run_condition, "node_id")
219                        else job_id
220                    ),
221                )
222
223                # Handle the result
224                self._handle_job_result(result, procedure)
225
226    def _handle_job_result(self, result, procedure: str) -> None:
227        """Handle the result of a completed job."""
228        if result.success and result.critical_point is not None:
229            # Handle successful job
230            if procedure == "upward":
231                # Add to graph (handles duplicates)
232                was_added = self.graph.add(result.critical_point)
233
234                if was_added:
235                    # Spawn new jobs from the new node
236                    new_node_id = result.critical_point.xyz
237                    new_jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(new_node_id, "upward")
238                    if new_jobs:
239                        self.job_queues.add_jobs("upward", new_jobs)
240                        logger.debug(
241                            f"Added new node {new_node_id} with {len(new_jobs)} new jobs"
242                        )
243                    # Trigger callback on graph change
244                    if self.callbacks is not None:
245                        for callback in self.callbacks:
246                            callback.on_job_complete(self)
247
248                # Mark job as complete immediately after HiSD run (for bookkeeping)
249                parent_node_id = self._get_parent_node_id(
250                    result.run_condition, result.job_id
251                )
252                logger.debug(
253                    f"DEBUG: Marking job complete - parent_node_id='{parent_node_id}', job_id='{result.job_id}'"
254                )
255                self.job_tracker.mark_job_complete(
256                    parent_node_id, result.job_id, result
257                )
258
259            elif procedure == "downward":
260                # Find or add the target node
261                target_node_id = self._find_or_add_target_node(result.critical_point)
262
263                # Get the source node that spawned this job
264                source_node_id = self._get_parent_node_id(
265                    result.run_condition, result.job_id
266                )
267
268                # Add edge between source and target (always, regardless of whether target was new)
269                self._add_edge_between_nodes(
270                    source_node_id, target_node_id, result.run_condition
271                )
272
273                # If target node was newly added, spawn jobs from it
274                if target_node_id == result.critical_point.xyz:  # It was newly added
275                    # Mark the new node as upward processed since it was found through downward search
276                    self.node_states.mark_processed(target_node_id, "upward")
277                    logger.debug(
278                        f"Marked new node {target_node_id} as upward processed (discovered via downward search)"
279                    )
280
281                    new_jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(target_node_id, "downward")
282                    if new_jobs:
283                        self.job_queues.add_jobs("downward", new_jobs)
284                        logger.debug(
285                            f"Added new node {target_node_id} with {len(new_jobs)} new jobs"
286                        )
287
288                # Trigger callbacks on graph change
289                if self.callbacks is not None:
290                    for callback in self.callbacks:
291                        callback.on_job_complete(self)
292
293                # Mark job as complete immediately after HiSD run (for bookkeeping)
294                logger.debug(
295                    f"DEBUG: Marking job complete - source_node_id='{source_node_id}', job_id='{result.job_id}'"
296                )
297                self.job_tracker.mark_job_complete(
298                    source_node_id, result.job_id, result
299                )
300
301            else:
302                raise ValueError(f"Unknown procedure: {procedure}")
303
304        else:
305            # Handle failed job (bookkeeping only)
306            logger.warning(f"Job {result.job_id} failed: {result.error}")
307            parent_node_id = self._get_parent_node_id(
308                result.run_condition, result.job_id
309            )
310            logger.debug(
311                f"DEBUG: Marking failed job complete - parent_node_id='{parent_node_id}', job_id='{result.job_id}'"
312            )
313            self.job_tracker.mark_job_complete(parent_node_id, result.job_id, result)
314
315    def _log_progress(self, procedure: str) -> None:
316        """Log current search progress."""
317        stats = self.node_states.get_processing_stats(procedure)
318        search_stats = self.monitor.search_stats.get(procedure)
319        jobs_executed = search_stats.total_jobs if search_stats else 0
320        logger.debug(
321            f"Progress: {stats['processed']}/{stats['total_nodes']} nodes processed, "
322            f"{self.job_queues.get_queue_length(procedure)} jobs queued, "
323            f"{jobs_executed} jobs executed"
324        )
325
326    def _finalize_search(self, procedure: str) -> None:
327        """Finalize search and log completion."""
328        # End monitoring the search
329        self.monitor.end_search(procedure)
330
331        # Get final statistics for logging
332        stats = self.monitor.search_stats.get(procedure)
333        if stats:
334            logger.debug(
335                f"{procedure.capitalize()} search completed in {stats.duration:.2f}s, "
336                f"{stats.total_jobs} jobs executed, {stats.completed_jobs} successful, "
337                f"{stats.failed_jobs} failed"
338            )
339
340    def is_upward_search_complete(self) -> bool:
341        """
342        Check if upward search is completely finished.
343
344        Returns:
345            True if upward job queue is empty AND all nodes have upward processing completed
346        """
347        upward_queue_empty = self.job_queues.is_queue_empty("upward")
348        all_nodes_upward_processed = not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(
349            "upward"
350        )
351
352        return upward_queue_empty and all_nodes_upward_processed
353
354    def is_downward_search_complete(self) -> bool:
355        """
356        Check if downward search is completely finished.
357
358        Returns:
359            True if downward job queue is empty AND all nodes have downward processing completed
360        """
361        downward_queue_empty = self.job_queues.is_queue_empty("downward")
362        all_nodes_downward_processed = not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(
363            "downward"
364        )
365
366        return downward_queue_empty and all_nodes_downward_processed
367
368    def run_downward_search(self) -> None:
369        """
370        Run the downward search algorithm using the downward strategy's
371        configured `perturbation_magnitude` that was set when the orchestrator
372        was initialized.
373        """
374        # Step 1: Synchronization check
375        if not self.is_upward_search_complete():
376            raise RuntimeError(
377                "Cannot start downward search: upward search is not complete"
378            )
379
380        # Step 2: preserve any loaded node state (no re-initialization)
381
382        self.run_search(self.downward_strategy, "downward")
383
384    def run_full_search(self) -> None:
385        """
386        Run the complete search algorithm: upward search followed by downward
387        search. Uses the strategies' configured perturbation magnitudes.
388        """
389        logger.debug("Starting full search (upward + downward)")
390
391        # Phase 1: Upward search
392        self.run_upward_search()
393
394        # Phase 2: Downward search (only if upward is complete)
395        if self.is_upward_search_complete():
396            self.run_downward_search()
397        else:
398            logger.error("Cannot proceed to downward search: upward search incomplete")
399
400        logger.debug("Full search completed")
401
402    def _check_and_mark_node_processed(self, node_id: str, procedure: str) -> None:
403        """
404        Check if a node has all its jobs completed and mark it as processed if so.
405
406        This method is called immediately after each job completion to ensure
407        nodes are marked processed without delay.
408
409        Args:
410            node_id: The node ID to check
411            procedure: The search procedure ('upward' or 'downward')
412        """
413        if self.job_tracker.all_jobs_complete(node_id):
414            self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
415            logger.debug(
416                f"✓ Node {node_id} fully processed immediately after job completion"
417            )
418
419    def _spawn_jobs_from_node(
420        self, node_id: str, procedure: str
421    ) -> List[tuple[str, RunCondition]]:
422        """Spawn jobs from a node using the configured strategy for the procedure.
423
424        Delegates the creation of RunConditions to the instantiated strategy
425        (`self.upward_strategy` or `self.downward_strategy`). Returns a list of
426        `(job_id, RunCondition)` tuples and registers the job ids with the
427        `job_tracker`.
428        """
429        if node_id not in self.graph._graph.nodes:
430            logger.warning(f"Node {node_id} not found in graph")
431            return []
432
433        node_data = self.graph._graph.nodes[node_id]["data"]
434
435        # Check d_max limit for upward search (orchestrator still authoritative)
436        if procedure == "upward" and self.d_max is not None:
437            if node_data.index >= self.d_max:
438                logger.debug(
439                    f"Node {node_id} has index {node_data.index} >= d_max ({self.d_max}), skipping upward job spawning"
440                )
441                return []
442
443        # Choose strategy for this procedure
444        if procedure == "upward":
445            strategy = self.upward_strategy
446        elif procedure == "downward":
447            strategy = self.downward_strategy
448        else:
449            logger.error(f"Unknown procedure: {procedure}")
450            return []
451
452        try:
453            run_conditions = strategy.spawn_jobs(node_data)
454        except Exception as e:
455            logger.error(f"Strategy.spawn_jobs failed for node {node_id}: {e}")
456            return []
457
458        if not run_conditions:
459            return []
460
461        # Create job ids and return job tuples
462        jobs: List[tuple[str, RunCondition]] = []
463        job_ids: List[str] = []
464        for idx, rc in enumerate(run_conditions):
465            job_id = f"{node_id}_{procedure}_{idx}"
466            jobs.append((job_id, rc))
467            job_ids.append(job_id)
468
469        # Track these jobs for the node
470        self.job_tracker.add_jobs_for_node(node_id, job_ids)
471
472        return jobs
473
474    def _get_parent_node_id(self, run_condition: RunCondition, job_id: str) -> str:
475        """
476        Get the parent node ID from a run condition and job ID.
477
478        The parent node ID is extracted from the job_id, which has the format:
479        "{parent_node_id}_{procedure}_{job_counter}"
480        """
481        # Extract parent node ID from job_id by finding the last occurrence of '_upward_' or '_downward_'
482        # and taking everything before that
483        if "_upward_" in job_id:
484            parent_node_id = job_id.rsplit("_upward_", 1)[0]
485        elif "_downward_" in job_id:
486            parent_node_id = job_id.rsplit("_downward_", 1)[0]
487        else:
488            # Fallback: use the XYZ from the run condition state
489            logger.warning(
490                f"Could not extract parent node ID from job_id {job_id}, falling back to XYZ computation"
491            )
492            parent_xyz = self.executor.hisd_runner.backend.get_xyz(run_condition.state)
493            return parent_xyz
494
495        return parent_node_id
496
497    def _find_or_add_target_node(self, critical_point: CriticalPoint) -> str:
498        """
499        Find an existing node matching the critical point, or add it as a new node.
500
501        Args:
502            critical_point: The critical point to find or add
503
504        Returns:
505            The node ID (XYZ string) of the found or added node
506        """
507        # Try to add the critical point (this will handle duplicates via distance)
508        was_added = self.graph.add(critical_point)
509
510        if was_added:
511            # It was a new node
512            return critical_point.xyz
513        else:
514            # It was a duplicate, find the existing node
515            # We need to search for a node with matching distance
516            target_node_id = None
517            for node_id, node_data in self.graph._graph.nodes(data=True):
518                if (
519                    self.graph.distance_function(
520                        critical_point.xyz,
521                        node_data["data"].xyz,
522                        **self.graph.distance_kwargs,
523                    )
524                    < self.graph.threshold
525                ):
526                    target_node_id = node_id
527                    break
528
529            if target_node_id is None:
530                logger.error(
531                    "Could not find existing node for duplicate critical point"
532                )
533                # Fallback: use the XYZ as ID anyway
534                target_node_id = critical_point.xyz
535
536            return target_node_id
537
538    def _add_edge_between_nodes(
539        self, source_node_id: str, target_node_id: str, run_condition: RunCondition
540    ) -> None:
541        """
542        Add an edge between source and target nodes with run condition metadata.
543
544        Args:
545            source_node_id: ID of the source node
546            target_node_id: ID of the target node
547            run_condition: The run condition that created this transition
548        """
549        # Add edge to the graph with metadata
550        edge_data = {
551            "run_condition": run_condition,
552            "direction": "downward",  # This is a downward transition
553            "created_at": time.time(),
554        }
555
556        self.graph._graph.add_edge(source_node_id, target_node_id, **edge_data)
557        logger.debug(f"Added downward edge from {source_node_id} to {target_node_id}")
558
559    def report(self) -> str:
560        """
561        Generate a comprehensive summary report of the orchestrator search status.
562
563        Returns:
564            str: Formatted summary report showing graph status, job queues,
565                 node processing status, and checkpoint contents preview
566        """
567        lines = []
568        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
569        lines.append("ORCHESTRATOR SEARCH STATUS SUMMARY")
570        lines.append("=" * 80)
571
572        # Graph status
573        lines.append("Graph Status:")
574        lines.append(f"  Total nodes: {len(self.graph._graph.nodes)}")
575        lines.append(f"  Total edges: {len(self.graph._graph.edges)}")
576
577        # Node breakdown by index
578        nodes_by_index = {}
579        for node_id, node_data in self.graph._graph.nodes(data=True):
580            point = node_data["data"]
581            index = point.index
582            if index not in nodes_by_index:
583                nodes_by_index[index] = []
584            nodes_by_index[index].append(point)
585
586        lines.append("  Nodes by Morse index:")
587        for index in sorted(nodes_by_index.keys()):
588            points = nodes_by_index[index]
589            coords_list = []
590            for point in points[:3]:  # Show first 3 points
591                coords = [round(float(c), 2) for c in point.state]
592                coords_list.append(f"[{coords[0]} {coords[1]} {coords[2]}]")
593            coords_str = ", ".join(coords_list)
594            if len(points) > 3:
595                coords_str += f" ... (+{len(points) - 3} more)"
596            lines.append(f"    Index {index}: {len(points)} points - {coords_str}")
597
598        # Job queue status
599        lines.append("\nJob Queue Status:")
600        total_pending_jobs = 0
601        queue_lengths = self.job_queues.get_all_queue_lengths()
602        for procedure, length in queue_lengths.items():
603            lines.append(f"  {procedure.capitalize()} queue: {length} pending jobs")
604            total_pending_jobs += length
605        lines.append(f"  Total pending jobs: {total_pending_jobs}")
606
607        # Node state status
608        lines.append("\nNode Processing Status:")
609        try:
610            processed_up = len(self.node_states.get_processed_nodes("upward"))
611            processed_down = len(self.node_states.get_processed_nodes("downward"))
612            unprocessed_up = len(self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes("upward"))
613            unprocessed_down = len(self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes("downward"))
614
615            lines.append(
616                f"  Upward search - Processed: {processed_up}, Unprocessed: {unprocessed_up}"
617            )
618            lines.append(
619                f"  Downward search - Processed: {processed_down}, Unprocessed: {unprocessed_down}"
620            )
621        except Exception as e:
622            lines.append(f"  Node state information not available: {e}")
623
624        lines.append("=" * 80)
625
626        return "\n".join(lines)
627
628    @classmethod
629    def load_checkpoint(
630        cls,
631        checkpoint_path: str,
632        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
633        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
634        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
635    ) -> "SearchOrchestrator":
636        """
637        Load a SearchOrchestrator from a checkpoint file.
638
639        Args:
640            checkpoint_path: Path to the checkpoint file
641            graph: The graph to use (should be loaded separately)
642            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner to use
643            callbacks: Optional callbacks instance to be notified after job batch execution
644
645        Returns:
646            SearchOrchestrator: Restored orchestrator instance
647        """
648        # Load checkpoint data using JSON checkpointer
649        json_checkpointer = CheckpointRegistry.create("json")
650        checkpoint_data = json_checkpointer.load(checkpoint_path)
651
652        # Restore graph from checkpoint
653        if "graph" in checkpoint_data:
654            graph = SearchableCriticalPointGraph.from_config(checkpoint_data["graph"])
655
656        # Create new orchestrator instance
657        orchestrator = cls(
658            graph=graph,
659            job_queues=JobQueues(),
660            hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
661            d_max=checkpoint_data.get("d_max"),
662            perturbation_magnitude=checkpoint_data.get("perturbation_magnitude", 0.1),
663            callbacks=callbacks,
664        )
665
666        # Restore job queues using JobQueues.from_config if present
667        raw_job_queues = checkpoint_data.get(
668            "job_queues", {"upward": [], "downward": []}
669        )
670        try:
671            orchestrator.job_queues = JobQueues.from_config(raw_job_queues)
672        except Exception:
673            # Fallback: manually reconstruct using RunCondition
674            from .search_primitives import RunCondition
675
676            orchestrator.job_queues = JobQueues()
677            for procedure, jobs in raw_job_queues.items():
678                reconstructed = [
679                    (job_id, RunCondition.from_config(run_condition_config))
680                    for job_id, run_condition_config in jobs
681                ]
682                orchestrator.job_queues._queues[procedure] = reconstructed
683
684        return orchestrator

Main orchestrator for search algorithms.

This class coordinates the entire search process, managing job queues, node states, and job execution according to the specified algorithm.

SearchOrchestrator( graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph, job_queues: src.dftscape.core.job_queues.JobQueues, hisd_runner: src.dftscape.core.interfaces.HiSDRunner, d_max: Optional[int] = None, perturbation_magnitude: float = 0.1, callbacks: Optional[List[src.dftscape.core.callbacks.OrchestratorCallback]] = None) 
 63    def __init__(
 64        self,
 65        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
 66        job_queues: JobQueues,
 67        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
 68        d_max: Optional[int] = None,
 69        perturbation_magnitude: float = 0.1,
 70        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
 71    ):
 72        """
 73        Initialize the search orchestrator.
 74
 75        Args:
 76            graph: The searchable graph to work with
 77            job_queues: The job queues for managing pending jobs
 78            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner for executing jobs
 79            d_max: Maximum search order (index) for upward search. If None, no limit is applied.
 80            perturbation_magnitude: Default magnitude for perturbations when spawning jobs
 81            callbacks: Optional callbacks instance to be notified after job batch execution
 82        """
 83        self.graph = graph
 84        self.job_queues = job_queues
 85        self.d_max = d_max
 86        self.job_tracker = JobTracker()
 87        self.node_states = NodeStateManager(graph)
 88        self.executor = JobExecutor(hisd_runner, max_concurrent=1)  # Start with serial
 89
 90        # Search parameters
 91        self.perturbation_magnitude = perturbation_magnitude
 92
 93        # Use composition with strategies (configured with default perturbation magnitude)
 94        self.upward_strategy = FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy(
 95            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
 96        )
 97        self.downward_strategy = ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy(
 98            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
 99        )
100
101        # Callbacks for job batch completion
102        self.callbacks = callbacks
103
104        # Statistics and monitoring
105        self.monitor: SearchMonitor = SearchMonitor()

Run the upward search algorithm using the upward strategy's configured perturbation_magnitude that was set when the orchestrator was initialized.

def run_search( self, strategy: src.dftscape.core.search_strategies.SearchStrategy, procedure: str) -> None: 
115    def run_search(self, strategy: "SearchStrategy", procedure: str) -> None:
116        """
117        Run a search using the given strategy.
118
119        Args:
120            strategy: The search strategy to use
121            procedure: The search procedure ("upward" or "downward")
122        """
123        self._initialize_search(procedure)
124
125        while not self._is_search_finished(procedure):
126            # For each unprocessed node, ask the strategy which RunConditions to spawn
127            unprocessed_nodes = self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
128            logger.debug(f"Found {len(unprocessed_nodes)} unprocessed nodes")
129
130            for node_id in unprocessed_nodes:
131                if node_id not in self.graph._graph.nodes:
132                    logger.warning(f"Node {node_id} not found in graph")
133                    self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
134                    continue
135
136                node_data = self.graph._graph.nodes[node_id]["data"]
137
138                # Delegation: strategy returns RunCondition objects for this critical point
139                try:
140                    run_conditions = strategy.spawn_jobs(node_data)
141                except Exception as e:
142                    logger.error(f"Strategy.spawn_jobs failed for node {node_id}: {e}")
143                    run_conditions = []
144
145                # Create job ids and register jobs
146                jobs: List[tuple[str, RunCondition]] = []
147                for idx, rc in enumerate(run_conditions):
148                    job_id = f"{node_id}_{procedure}_{idx}"
149                    jobs.append((job_id, rc))
150
151                # Add to queues and tracker
152                self.job_queues.add_jobs(procedure, jobs)
153                job_ids = [job_id for job_id, _ in jobs]
154                self.job_tracker.add_jobs_for_node(node_id, job_ids)
155                # Mark node processed immediately after spawning and registering jobs
156                self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
157
158            # Execute pending jobs and log progress
159            self._execute_pending_jobs(procedure)
160            self._log_progress(procedure)
161
162        self._finalize_search(procedure)

Run a search using the given strategy.

Args: strategy: The search strategy to use procedure: The search procedure ("upward" or "downward")

def is_upward_search_complete(self) -> bool: 
340    def is_upward_search_complete(self) -> bool:
341        """
342        Check if upward search is completely finished.
343

345            True if upward job queue is empty AND all nodes have upward processing completed
346        """
347        upward_queue_empty = self.job_queues.is_queue_empty("upward")
348        all_nodes_upward_processed = not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(
349            "upward"
350        )
351
352        return upward_queue_empty and all_nodes_upward_processed

def run_downward_search(self) -> None: 
368    def run_downward_search(self) -> None:
369        """
370        Run the downward search algorithm using the downward strategy's
371        configured `perturbation_magnitude` that was set when the orchestrator
372        was initialized.
373        """
374        # Step 1: Synchronization check
375        if not self.is_upward_search_complete():
376            raise RuntimeError(
377                "Cannot start downward search: upward search is not complete"
378            )
379
380        # Step 2: preserve any loaded node state (no re-initialization)
381
382        self.run_search(self.downward_strategy, "downward")

Run the downward search algorithm using the downward strategy's configured perturbation_magnitude that was set when the orchestrator was initialized.

def run_full_search(self) -> None: 
384    def run_full_search(self) -> None:
385        """
386        Run the complete search algorithm: upward search followed by downward
387        search. Uses the strategies' configured perturbation magnitudes.
388        """
389        logger.debug("Starting full search (upward + downward)")
390
391        # Phase 1: Upward search
392        self.run_upward_search()
393
394        # Phase 2: Downward search (only if upward is complete)
395        if self.is_upward_search_complete():
396            self.run_downward_search()
397        else:
398            logger.error("Cannot proceed to downward search: upward search incomplete")
399
400        logger.debug("Full search completed")

Run the complete search algorithm: upward search followed by downward search. Uses the strategies' configured perturbation magnitudes.

def report(self) -> str: 
559    def report(self) -> str:
560        """
561        Generate a comprehensive summary report of the orchestrator search status.
562
563        Returns:
564            str: Formatted summary report showing graph status, job queues,
565                 node processing status, and checkpoint contents preview
566        """
567        lines = []
568        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
569        lines.append("ORCHESTRATOR SEARCH STATUS SUMMARY")
570        lines.append("=" * 80)
571
572        # Graph status
573        lines.append("Graph Status:")
574        lines.append(f"  Total nodes: {len(self.graph._graph.nodes)}")
575        lines.append(f"  Total edges: {len(self.graph._graph.edges)}")
576
577        # Node breakdown by index
578        nodes_by_index = {}
579        for node_id, node_data in self.graph._graph.nodes(data=True):
580            point = node_data["data"]
581            index = point.index
582            if index not in nodes_by_index:
583                nodes_by_index[index] = []
584            nodes_by_index[index].append(point)
585
586        lines.append("  Nodes by Morse index:")
587        for index in sorted(nodes_by_index.keys()):
588            points = nodes_by_index[index]
589            coords_list = []
590            for point in points[:3]:  # Show first 3 points
591                coords = [round(float(c), 2) for c in point.state]
592                coords_list.append(f"[{coords[0]} {coords[1]} {coords[2]}]")
593            coords_str = ", ".join(coords_list)
594            if len(points) > 3:
595                coords_str += f" ... (+{len(points) - 3} more)"
596            lines.append(f"    Index {index}: {len(points)} points - {coords_str}")
597
598        # Job queue status
599        lines.append("\nJob Queue Status:")
600        total_pending_jobs = 0
601        queue_lengths = self.job_queues.get_all_queue_lengths()
602        for procedure, length in queue_lengths.items():
603            lines.append(f"  {procedure.capitalize()} queue: {length} pending jobs")
604            total_pending_jobs += length
605        lines.append(f"  Total pending jobs: {total_pending_jobs}")
606
607        # Node state status
608        lines.append("\nNode Processing Status:")
609        try:
610            processed_up = len(self.node_states.get_processed_nodes("upward"))
611            processed_down = len(self.node_states.get_processed_nodes("downward"))
612            unprocessed_up = len(self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes("upward"))
613            unprocessed_down = len(self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes("downward"))
614
615            lines.append(
616                f"  Upward search - Processed: {processed_up}, Unprocessed: {unprocessed_up}"
617            )
618            lines.append(
619                f"  Downward search - Processed: {processed_down}, Unprocessed: {unprocessed_down}"
620            )
621        except Exception as e:
622            lines.append(f"  Node state information not available: {e}")
623
624        lines.append("=" * 80)
625
626        return "\n".join(lines)

Generate a comprehensive summary report of the orchestrator search status.

Returns: str: Formatted summary report showing graph status, job queues, node processing status, and checkpoint contents preview

@classmethod
def load_checkpoint( cls, checkpoint_path: str, graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph, hisd_runner: src.dftscape.core.interfaces.HiSDRunner, callbacks: Optional[List[src.dftscape.core.callbacks.OrchestratorCallback]] = None) -> SearchOrchestrator: 
628    @classmethod
629    def load_checkpoint(
630        cls,
631        checkpoint_path: str,
632        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
633        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
634        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
635    ) -> "SearchOrchestrator":
636        """
637        Load a SearchOrchestrator from a checkpoint file.
638
639        Args:
640            checkpoint_path: Path to the checkpoint file
641            graph: The graph to use (should be loaded separately)
642            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner to use
643            callbacks: Optional callbacks instance to be notified after job batch execution
644
645        Returns:
646            SearchOrchestrator: Restored orchestrator instance
647        """
648        # Load checkpoint data using JSON checkpointer
649        json_checkpointer = CheckpointRegistry.create("json")
650        checkpoint_data = json_checkpointer.load(checkpoint_path)
651
652        # Restore graph from checkpoint
653        if "graph" in checkpoint_data:
654            graph = SearchableCriticalPointGraph.from_config(checkpoint_data["graph"])
655
656        # Create new orchestrator instance
657        orchestrator = cls(
658            graph=graph,
659            job_queues=JobQueues(),
660            hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
661            d_max=checkpoint_data.get("d_max"),
662            perturbation_magnitude=checkpoint_data.get("perturbation_magnitude", 0.1),
663            callbacks=callbacks,
664        )
665
666        # Restore job queues using JobQueues.from_config if present
667        raw_job_queues = checkpoint_data.get(
668            "job_queues", {"upward": [], "downward": []}
669        )
670        try:
671            orchestrator.job_queues = JobQueues.from_config(raw_job_queues)
672        except Exception:
673            # Fallback: manually reconstruct using RunCondition
674            from .search_primitives import RunCondition
675
676            orchestrator.job_queues = JobQueues()
677            for procedure, jobs in raw_job_queues.items():
678                reconstructed = [
679                    (job_id, RunCondition.from_config(run_condition_config))
680                    for job_id, run_condition_config in jobs
681                ]
682                orchestrator.job_queues._queues[procedure] = reconstructed
683
684        return orchestrator

Load a SearchOrchestrator from a checkpoint file.

Args: checkpoint_path: Path to the checkpoint file graph: The graph to use (should be loaded separately) hisd_runner: The HiSD runner to use callbacks: Optional callbacks instance to be notified after job batch execution

Returns: SearchOrchestrator: Restored orchestrator instance

class JobTracker: 
 19class JobTracker:
 20    """
 21    Tracks job completion and dependencies for nodes.
 22
 23    This class maintains the relationship between nodes and the jobs spawned from them,
 24    allowing the orchestrator to know when all jobs from a node have completed.
 25    """
 26
 27    def __init__(self):
 28        # node_id -> set of job_ids that were spawned from this node
 29        self.pending_jobs: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {}
 30        # node_id -> set of job_ids that have completed
 31        self.completed_jobs: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {}
 32        # job_id -> JobResult for completed jobs
 33        self.job_results: Dict[str, JobResult] = {}
 34
 35    def add_jobs_for_node(self, node_id: str, job_ids: List[str]) -> None:
 36        """Track jobs that were spawned from a node."""
 37        if node_id not in self.pending_jobs:
 38            self.pending_jobs[node_id] = set()
 39        if node_id not in self.completed_jobs:
 40            self.completed_jobs[node_id] = set()
 41
 42        self.pending_jobs[node_id].update(job_ids)
 43        logger.debug(f"Added {len(job_ids)} jobs for node {node_id}")
 44
 45    def mark_job_complete(self, node_id: str, job_id: str, result: JobResult) -> None:
 46        """Mark a job as completed and store the result."""
 47        # Normalize job_id to string
 48        job_id_str = str(job_id)
 49
 50        # If already completed, skip
 51        if job_id_str in self.job_results:
 52            logger.debug(f"Job {job_id_str} already completed, skipping")
 53            return
 54
 55        # Direct hit
 56        if node_id in self.pending_jobs and job_id_str in self.pending_jobs[node_id]:
 57            self.pending_jobs[node_id].remove(job_id_str)
 58            self.completed_jobs[node_id].add(job_id_str)
 59            self.job_results[job_id_str] = result
 60            logger.debug(f"✓ Job {job_id_str} completed for node {node_id}")
 61            return
 62
 63        # Fallback: sometimes callers pass only a numeric suffix (e.g. '1') instead
 64        # of the full job id 'node_upward_1'. Try to match by suffix within pending.
 65        pending_for_node = self.pending_jobs.get(node_id, set())
 66        if pending_for_node:
 67            # Look for any pending job that ends with the provided id
 68            candidate = None
 69            for pj in pending_for_node:
 70                if pj == job_id_str:
 71                    candidate = pj
 72                    break
 73                # match suffix like '_1' or '_upward_1' -> split last token
 74                try:
 75                    last_token = pj.rsplit("_", 1)[-1]
 76                except Exception:
 77                    last_token = pj
 78                if last_token == job_id_str:
 79                    candidate = pj
 80                    break
 81
 82            if candidate is not None:
 83                # Use the matched candidate id for bookkeeping
 84                self.pending_jobs[node_id].remove(candidate)
 85                self.completed_jobs.setdefault(node_id, set()).add(candidate)
 86                self.job_results[candidate] = result
 87                logger.debug(
 88                    f"✓ Job {candidate} (matched from '{job_id_str}') completed for node {node_id}"
 89                )
 90                return
 91
 92        # Nothing matched - provide diagnostic context in the warning
 93        logger.warning(
 94            f"✗ Attempted to mark unknown job {job_id_str} as complete for node {node_id}."
 95            f" Pending jobs for node: {sorted(list(pending_for_node))}"
 96        )
 97
 98    def all_jobs_complete(self, node_id: str) -> bool:
 99        """Check if all jobs spawned from a node have completed."""
100        pending = self.pending_jobs.get(node_id, set())
101        return len(pending) == 0
102
103    def get_pending_job_count(self, node_id: str) -> int:
104        """Get the number of pending jobs for a node."""
105        return len(self.pending_jobs.get(node_id, set()))
106
107    def get_completed_job_count(self, node_id: str) -> int:
108        """Get the number of completed jobs for a node."""
109        return len(self.completed_jobs.get(node_id, set()))
110
111    def get_job_result(self, job_id: str) -> Optional[JobResult]:
112        """Get the result of a completed job."""
113        return self.job_results.get(job_id)
114
115    def get_failed_jobs(self, node_id: str) -> List[str]:
116        """Get list of failed jobs for a node."""
117        failed = []
118        for job_id in self.completed_jobs.get(node_id, set()):
119            result = self.job_results.get(job_id)
120            if result and not result.success:
121                failed.append(job_id)
122        return failed

19class NodeStateManager:
20    """
21    Manages the processing state of nodes for different search procedures.
22
23    This class provides a clean interface to the SearchableCriticalPointGraph's
24    state management methods, with additional utilities for the orchestrator.
25    """
26
27    def __init__(self, graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph):
28        self.graph = graph
29
30    def get_unprocessed_nodes(self, procedure: str) -> List[str]:
31        """Get nodes that haven't been processed by this procedure."""
32        return list(self.graph.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure))
33
34    def get_processed_nodes(self, procedure: str) -> List[str]:
35        """Get nodes that have been processed by this procedure."""
36        processed = []
37        for node_id in self.graph._graph.nodes:
38            if self.graph.is_processed(node_id, procedure):
39                processed.append(node_id)
40        return processed
41
42    def mark_processed(self, node_id: str, procedure: str) -> None:
43        """Mark a node as fully processed by a procedure."""
44        self.graph.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
45        logger.debug(f"Marked node {node_id} as processed for {procedure}")
46
47    def is_processed(self, node_id: str, procedure: str) -> bool:
48        """Check if a node has been processed by a procedure."""
49        return self.graph.is_processed(node_id, procedure)
50
51    def get_processing_stats(self, procedure: str) -> Dict[str, int]:
52        """Get processing statistics for a procedure."""
53        return self.graph.get_processing_stats(procedure)
54
55    def has_unprocessed_nodes(self, procedure: str) -> bool:
56        """Check if there are any unprocessed nodes for a procedure."""
57        return len(self.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)) > 0

class JobExecutor: 
21class JobExecutor:
22    """
23    Handles the execution of jobs, supporting both serial and parallel modes.
24
25    This class abstracts the execution logic, making it easy to switch between
26    serial and parallel execution modes.
27    """
28
29    def __init__(self, hisd_runner: HiSDRunner, max_concurrent: int = 1):
30        """
31        Initialize the job executor.
32
33        Args:
34            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner that executes RunCondition -> CriticalPoint
35            max_concurrent: Maximum number of concurrent jobs (1 for serial)
36        """
37        self.hisd_runner = hisd_runner
38        self.max_concurrent = max_concurrent
39
40    def execute_job(self, run_condition: RunCondition, job_id: str) -> JobResult:
41        """Execute a single job and return the result."""
42        start_time = time.time()
43
44        try:
45            critical_point = self.hisd_runner.run(run_condition)
46            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
47
48            if critical_point is None:
49                # HiSD failed to converge within maxiter
50                result = JobResult(
51                    job_id=job_id,
52                    run_condition=run_condition,
53                    critical_point=None,
54                    success=False,
55                    error="HiSD failed to converge.",
56                    execution_time=execution_time,
57                )
58                return result
59
60            result = JobResult(
61                job_id=job_id,
62                run_condition=run_condition,
63                critical_point=critical_point,
64                success=True,
65                execution_time=execution_time,
66            )
67
68            return result
69
70        except Exception as e:
71            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
72            error_msg = f"Job execution failed: {str(e)}"
73
74            result = JobResult(
75                job_id=job_id,
76                run_condition=run_condition,
77                success=False,
78                error=error_msg,

def execute_job( self, run_condition: RunCondition, job_id: str) -> src.dftscape.core.job_result.JobResult: 
40    def execute_job(self, run_condition: RunCondition, job_id: str) -> JobResult:
41        """Execute a single job and return the result."""
42        start_time = time.time()
43
44        try:
45            critical_point = self.hisd_runner.run(run_condition)
46            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
47
48            if critical_point is None:
49                # HiSD failed to converge within maxiter
50                result = JobResult(
51                    job_id=job_id,
52                    run_condition=run_condition,
53                    critical_point=None,
54                    success=False,
55                    error="HiSD failed to converge.",
56                    execution_time=execution_time,
57                )
58                return result
59
60            result = JobResult(
61                job_id=job_id,
62                run_condition=run_condition,
63                critical_point=critical_point,
64                success=True,
65                execution_time=execution_time,
66            )
67
68            return result
69
70        except Exception as e:
71            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
72            error_msg = f"Job execution failed: {str(e)}"
73
74            result = JobResult(
75                job_id=job_id,
76                run_condition=run_condition,
77                success=False,
78                error=error_msg,
79                execution_time=execution_time,
80            )
81
82            logger.error(f"Job {job_id} failed: {error_msg}")
83            return result
